When these snacks and drinks were born.Dr Pepper: The Texas pharmacist's drink debuted a year before Coca-Cola, and Dr Pepper claims to be the oldest major soft drink in America.
When these snacks and drinks were born.Jell-O: Inventor Pearle Wait sold the rights to the gelatin dessert for a few hundred dollars, and it later became a household name.
When these snacks and drinks were born.Hershey's milk chocolate bar: Milton Hershey made his fortune on caramels first, then built a company town in Pennsylvania for his chocolate workers.
When these snacks and drinks were born.Oreo: Nabisco's sandwich cookie has outsold every other cookie in the world, with billions made each year.
When these snacks and drinks were born.Twinkie: Baker James Dewar invented the cream-filled sponge cake, and it was originally filled with banana cream, until wartime shortages.
When these snacks and drinks were born.Chocolate chip cookie: Ruth Wakefield invented it at the Toll House Inn in Massachusetts, supposedly adding chopped chocolate to dough.
When these snacks and drinks were born.M&M's: Forrest Mars modeled them on British Smarties, and the candy-coated shell kept chocolate from melting in soldiers' hands.
When these snacks and drinks were born.Cheetos: Frito-Lay's cheesy corn snack came from a cornmeal extruder, and its orange cheese dust famously stains fingers.
When these snacks and drinks were born.Pop-Tarts: Kellogg's toaster pastry raced to beat a rival's product to market, and its original flavors were fruit-filled.
When these snacks and drinks were born.Red Bull: Dietrich Mateschitz of Austria based it on a Thai drink called Krating Daeng, and the name Red Bull is a translation.

Anime TV series premieres in Japan.Astro Boy: Osamu Tezuka's series was Japan's first TV anime, and its limited animation helped set the style for decades.
Anime TV series premieres in Japan.Speed Racer: Called Mach GoGoGo in Japan, it was dubbed for US audiences and became one of the first anime hits abroad.
Anime TV series premieres in Japan.Mobile Suit Gundam: Its low ratings led to cancellation, but model kits called Gunpla later made it a franchise bigger than the show.
Anime TV series premieres in Japan.Dragon Ball: Akira Toriyama's series was loosely inspired by the Chinese classic Journey to the West.
Anime TV series premieres in Japan.Sailor Moon: Naoko Takeuchi's heroine defined the magical-girl genre and became a global phenomenon.
Anime TV series premieres in Japan.Neon Genesis Evangelion: Hideaki Anno's tale of giant robots and troubled pilots reshaped anime in the 1990s and boosted its studio, Gainax.
Anime TV series premieres in Japan.Pokémon: An episode in December 1997 flashed lights that caused seizures in hundreds of Japanese viewers and led to broadcast safety guidelines.
Anime TV series premieres in Japan.One Piece: Eiichiro Oda's pirate saga is the best-selling manga series of all time.
Anime TV series premieres in Japan.Naruto: Masashi Kishimoto's ninja saga gave the world the Naruto run, with arms swept back.
Anime TV series premieres in Japan.Attack on Titan: Hajime Isayama's tale of giants and walled cities ended in 2023 after a ten-year run.

How many? From guitar strings to leap da.Strings on a guitar: Standard tuning from low to high is E A D G B E, and many guitars also come in twelve-string versions with doubled strings.
How many? From guitar strings to leap da.Legs on a spider: Spiders have eight legs and are arachnids, unlike insects, which have six; they also have no antennae and two body sections.
How many? From guitar strings to leap da.Players on a soccer team: Cricket also fields this many, and the number was settled in 19th-century England when football was codified.
How many? From guitar strings to leap da.Dots on a die (total): Opposite faces always add up to seven, so the one is opposite the six, and the dots on a die total 21.
How many? From guitar strings to leap da.Adult human teeth: The total includes four wisdom teeth, which many people never develop or have removed; children have only 20 baby teeth.
How many? From guitar strings to leap da.Cards in a deck (no jokers): Four suits of 13 ranks make up the deck, and the number of possible shuffled orderings is about 8 followed by 67 zeros.
How many? From guitar strings to leap da.Squares on a chessboard: A legend says putting one grain on the first square and doubling for each next would produce more rice than the world has grown.
How many? From guitar strings to leap da.Keys on a piano: A standard piano has 52 white keys and 36 black ones, covering seven octaves and a bit.
How many? From guitar strings to leap da.Bones in an adult human: Babies are born with about 300 bones, and many fuse together as they grow, leaving the adult number.
How many? From guitar strings to leap da.Days in a leap year: The extra day is added on February 29 because Earth's orbit takes about 365.24 days, so calendars need a leap day to keep up.

Bright stars from far north to far south.Polaris: Polaris sits almost over Earth's north pole, so it stays almost fixed in the sky while others circle around it.
Bright stars from far north to far south.Capella: Capella is actually a system of four stars, and it is one of the brightest in the northern sky.
Bright stars from far north to far south.Vega: Vega was the northern pole star about 12,000 years ago, and it will be again, thanks to Earth's wobbling axis.
Bright stars from far north to far south.Arcturus: Arcturus is a red giant, and it is the brightest star in the northern celestial hemisphere.
Bright stars from far north to far south.Altair: Altair spins so fast that it is squashed into an oval shape, and it completes a rotation in about nine hours.
Bright stars from far north to far south.Rigel: Rigel is a blue supergiant tens of thousands of times as luminous as the Sun, and it marks Orion's foot.
Bright stars from far north to far south.Sirius: Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky, and its name comes from the Greek for scorching.
Bright stars from far north to far south.Antares: Antares is a red supergiant whose name means rival of Mars, because of their similar reddish color.
Bright stars from far north to far south.Canopus: Canopus is the second-brightest star in the night sky, and it is used by spacecraft for navigation.
Bright stars from far north to far south.Acrux (Southern Cross): Acrux is the brightest star of the Southern Cross, and the constellation appears on the flags of Australia and New Zealand.

When these Google products launched.Google Search: It began as a project called BackRub at Stanford, run by Larry Page and Sergey Brin.
When these Google products launched.AdWords: It sold ads linked to search keywords, and became the main engine of the company's revenue.
When these Google products launched.Gmail: It launched on April Fools' Day 2004 with a gigabyte of storage, so many people thought it was a joke.
When these Google products launched.Google Maps: Built on acquired startups, it was soon followed by satellite imagery and Street View, launched in 2007.
When these Google products launched.Chrome: Its launch was announced with a comic book drawn by Scott McCloud, and it was built on open-source Chromium.
When these Google products launched.Google+: Google's social network, shut down in 2019 after low use and a data security bug.
When these Google products launched.Chromecast: A 35 dollar dongle that lets phones send videos to a TV.
When these Google products launched.Pixel phone: It replaced the earlier Nexus line, and was Google's first phone built under its own brand.
When these Google products launched.Stadia: A cloud gaming service that streamed games to screens, and was shut down in January 2023.
When these Google products launched.Bard: The AI chatbot was later renamed Gemini in 2024.

Olympic weightlifting plates by colour.Small white plate: Competition plates are colour-coded by weight, and the smallest ones let lifters make tiny jumps at record attempts.
Olympic weightlifting plates by colour.Small green plate: By international colour code, green means 10 kg on big plates and 1 kg on small ones.
Olympic weightlifting plates by colour.Small yellow plate: Yellow marks 15 kg on big plates and 1.5 kg on small ones, so referees can verify loads at a glance.
Olympic weightlifting plates by colour.Small blue plate: Blue is 20 kg on big plates, so this small blue disc is a tenth of that for fine increments.
Olympic weightlifting plates by colour.Small red plate: Red is the heaviest class at 25 kg, and the small red one at 2.5 kg is the biggest of the small-change plates.
Olympic weightlifting plates by colour.Big white plate: Identical colour coding makes every competition bar look standard, so officials can confirm loads from a distance.
Olympic weightlifting plates by colour.Big green plate: A men's Olympic bar weighs 20 kg and a women's 15 kg, so one green pair adds 20 kg.
Olympic weightlifting plates by colour.Big yellow plate: A pair of these plus a 20 kg men's bar makes 50 kg, an easy warm-up load.
Olympic weightlifting plates by colour.Big blue plate: Blue means this plate weighs 20 kg, so a pair plus the bar totals 60 kg.
Olympic weightlifting plates by colour.Big red plate: Elite lifters stack many of these, since world-record lifts exceed 250 kg.

Scientists who became units, by birth ye.Isaac Newton: Newton described gravity and three laws of motion, and the unit of force is named for him, where one newton is about the weight of a small apple.
Scientists who became units, by birth ye.Anders Celsius: He proposed a temperature scale in 1742, but initially had boiling at 0 and freezing at 100 degrees, and someone flipped it after his death.
Scientists who became units, by birth ye.James Watt: His improvements to the steam engine made it far more efficient, and he coined 'horsepower' to help sell engines to mill owners.
Scientists who became units, by birth ye.Alessandro Volta: This Italian physicist invented the voltaic pile, the first chemical battery, in 1800, and Napoleon made him a count for it.
Scientists who became units, by birth ye.André-Marie Ampère: Ampère founded electromagnetism within weeks of hearing of Ørsted's discovery, and Maxwell later called him the Newton of electricity.
Scientists who became units, by birth ye.Georg Ohm: A German physicist whose law relates voltage, current and resistance, he was first ignored, and his work was ridiculed by critics.
Scientists who became units, by birth ye.Michael Faraday: A self-taught English bookbinder's apprentice, he discovered electromagnetic induction, and also gave Royal Institution Christmas lectures for children that still run today.
Scientists who became units, by birth ye.James Joule: A brewer's son from Manchester, he showed that heat and work are equivalent, and the joule is named for him; one joule is a very small amount of energy.
Scientists who became units, by birth ye.Lord Kelvin: William Thomson was made a lord, and the temperature scale named for him starts at absolute zero, about minus 273.15 degrees Celsius.
Scientists who became units, by birth ye.Heinrich Hertz: He first proved the existence of radio waves in the 1880s, and the unit of frequency, one cycle per second, honors him.

How old these monarchs were when they to.Mary, Queen of Scots: Mary became queen of Scotland at six days old after her father James V died, and she was sent to France as a child.
How old these monarchs were when they to.Puyi, last emperor of China: Puyi became emperor at two in 1908, and later was installed as puppet ruler of Manchukuo; his life inspired the film The Last Emperor.
How old these monarchs were when they to.Louis XIV: Louis XIV became king at four in 1643, and he reigned for 72 years, longer than any other major European monarch, and called himself the Sun King.
How old these monarchs were when they to.Edward VI: The son of Henry VIII and Jane Seymour was nine years old when he became king, and was a devout Protestant, but he died at fifteen.
How old these monarchs were when they to.Queen Victoria: The 18-year-old woke before dawn to learn she was queen, and her 63-year reign gave its name to a whole era.
How old these monarchs were when they to.Elizabeth I: She took the throne at 25 on her half-sister Mary's death, and her reign saw Shakespeare, Drake and the Armada's defeat.
How old these monarchs were when they to.Catherine the Great: Born a German princess, she seized the Russian throne at 33 after a coup against her husband, and she expanded the empire's borders.
How old these monarchs were when they to.Queen Anne: She came to the throne at 37, and she was the last Stuart ruler; the Treaty of Union made her the first monarch of Great Britain.
How old these monarchs were when they to.Edward VII: Queen Victoria's son waited 59 years to become king, and he was the oldest heir at the time, as well as the first monarch of the House of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha.
How old these monarchs were when they to.William IV: The 'Sailor King' took the throne at 64, after serving in the Royal Navy, and was the oldest person at the time to become a British monarch.

Asian cities from west to east.Istanbul: It straddles two continents across the Bosphorus, and it is Europe's largest city by population, though its center lies on the European side.
Asian cities from west to east.Tehran: It lies at the foot of the Alborz mountains, and snow-capped peaks are visible from the city on clear days, including Mount Damavand.
Asian cities from west to east.Dubai: It is home to the Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building at over 800 m, which was completed in 2010 and holds many records.
Asian cities from west to east.Karachi: It is Pakistan's largest city and main port on the Arabian Sea, and it lies near the mouth of the Indus River delta.
Asian cities from west to east.New Delhi: Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker designed it as the new capital of British India, inaugurated in 1931, with wide avenues.
Asian cities from west to east.Kathmandu: It lies in a valley at about 1,400 m and is a gateway for expeditions to Everest and the many peaks of the Himalayas.
Asian cities from west to east.Bangkok: Its ceremonial name is among the longest city names in the world, and begins with Krung Thep Maha Nakhon, City of Angels.
Asian cities from west to east.Beijing: The Forbidden City, with about 980 buildings, was home to emperors for about 500 years and is today a museum.
Asian cities from west to east.Seoul: About half of South Korea's population lives in the capital region, which makes it among the world's densest metropolitan areas.
Asian cities from west to east.Vladivostok: It is the eastern end of the Trans-Siberian Railway, 9,289 km from Moscow, and the journey crosses seven time zones.

Arctic animals by weight.Arctic tern: It migrates from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back, a round trip of around 70,000 km, so it sees more daylight than any other animal.
Arctic animals by weight.Rock ptarmigan: This grouse turns from brown in summer to white in winter, and grows feathered feet that work like snowshoes.
Arctic animals by weight.Arctic fox: Its coat turns from brown to white in winter, and its fur is among the best insulation of any mammal, so it can curl up and sleep through blizzards.
Arctic animals by weight.Wolverine: Despite looking like a small bear, it's a weasel relative. It is strong enough to drive wolves off a kill and can crunch frozen bones.
Arctic animals by weight.Arctic wolf: A subspecies of the gray wolf living far north, it often hunts muskoxen in packs and can go weeks between large meals.
Arctic animals by weight.Caribou: In North America this is the name for the wild reindeer. Both sexes grow antlers, unusual for deer, and herds migrate thousands of kilometers.
Arctic animals by weight.Muskox: Its dense wool, called qiviut, is softer than cashmere and eight times as warm as sheep's wool. When threatened, adults form a circle around calves.
Arctic animals by weight.Polar bear (male): The largest land carnivore on Earth. Its fur looks white but the hairs are actually clear and hollow, and the skin beneath is black.
Arctic animals by weight.Beluga: This white whale is closely related to the narwhal and spends summers in Arctic estuaries. It can even swim backwards, which few whales manage.
Arctic animals by weight.Bowhead whale: It can live for over 200 years, perhaps the longest of any mammal, and uses its giant skull to break through sea ice about a meter thick.

Islamic observances through the Hijri ye.Islamic New Year: The first month of the Islamic lunar calendar is one of four sacred months, when fighting is forbidden.
Islamic observances through the Hijri ye.Ashura: It is the tenth day of Muharram, and it is observed by fasting in remembrance of when Moses was saved from Pharaoh.
Islamic observances through the Hijri ye.Mawlid an-Nabi: Muslims mark the birthday of the Prophet in the month of Rabi al-Awwal, and the date is also traditionally linked with his death.
Islamic observances through the Hijri ye.Isra and Mi'raj: The Night Journey and Ascension is when the Prophet travelled to Jerusalem and then to heaven, where the five daily prayers were established.
Islamic observances through the Hijri ye.Mid-Sha'ban: The night is marked by prayer and forgiveness, and it is a night believed to be a time when fates are decided for the year.
Islamic observances through the Hijri ye.Start of the fast: The month of fasting starts when the new crescent moon is seen, and so the date can vary by a day or two.
Islamic observances through the Hijri ye.Laylat al-Qadr: The 'Night of Power' is when the Quran was first revealed, and it is believed to be better than a thousand months.
Islamic observances through the Hijri ye.Eid al-Fitr: The 'Festival of Breaking the Fast' follows a month of fasting, and the day begins with a special prayer and charity.
Islamic observances through the Hijri ye.Day of Arafah: This day of the pilgrimage is when pilgrims gather on a plain near Mecca, and fasting on it is said to erase two years of sins.
Islamic observances through the Hijri ye.Eid al-Adha: The 'Festival of Sacrifice' commemorates Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son, and families share meat with the poor.

Top speeds of these connections.Dial-up modem: The screeching handshake of a 56k modem was two machines negotiating a line, and 56 kbps was rarely reached in practice.
Top speeds of these connections.ISDN line: ISDN bonded two 64 kbps digital channels over ordinary copper phone lines, giving 128 kbps.
Top speeds of these connections.USB 1.1: The 1998 iMac dropped older ports and relied on USB, which helped make the standard mainstream.
Top speeds of these connections.Fast Ethernet: It ended the era of shared 10 Mbps office networks and ran over ordinary twisted-pair cable.
Top speeds of these connections.USB 2.0: Its 480 Mbps 'Hi-Speed' figure was a theoretical maximum; real transfers were far slower.
Top speeds of these connections.Gigabit Ethernet: Gigabit over ordinary copper made wired networking fast enough for homes, still within a 100 m cable limit.
Top speeds of these connections.USB 3.0: Its 'SuperSpeed' ports are often marked in blue, and it cut the time to copy big files dramatically.
Top speeds of these connections.USB 3.1 Gen 2: Repeated renaming, including 'USB 3.2 Gen 2', confused buyers about which speed they were actually getting.
Top speeds of these connections.Thunderbolt 3: Intel developed it with Apple, and it carries video, data and power over one USB-C cable.
Top speeds of these connections.USB4 Version 2.0: Announced in 2022, it doubles USB4's 40 Gbps, with an asymmetric mode reaching 120 Gbps in one direction.

Scientific hoaxes and frauds, in order.Beringer's lying stones: His 'fossils' were carved by colleagues who wanted to embarrass him, and he published a book about them.
Scientific hoaxes and frauds, in order.Great Moon Hoax: The New York Sun claimed an astronomer saw bat-winged people on the Moon, wrongly attributing it to John Herschel.
Scientific hoaxes and frauds, in order.Feejee mermaid: P.T. Barnum exhibited what was really a monkey's upper body stitched to a fish's tail.
Scientific hoaxes and frauds, in order.Cardiff Giant: George Hull buried a carved gypsum 'petrified man' to mock literal readers of the Bible, and Barnum made a copy.
Scientific hoaxes and frauds, in order.N-rays: René Blondlot claimed to see these rays until Robert Wood secretly removed a key prism during a demonstration.
Scientific hoaxes and frauds, in order.Piltdown Man: This fake skull passed as the 'missing link' for about 40 years, until tests in 1953 exposed it.
Scientific hoaxes and frauds, in order.Cold fusion: Pons and Fleischmann announced it at a press conference, but other labs could not reproduce the results.
Scientific hoaxes and frauds, in order.Sokal hoax: Physicist Alan Sokal submitted a nonsense paper to Social Text, and it was published.
Scientific hoaxes and frauds, in order.Wakefield's MMR paper: He falsified data linking the MMR vaccine to autism, and was struck off the medical register.
Scientific hoaxes and frauds, in order.Hwang's cloning fraud: The South Korean scientist faked human embryonic stem cell lines, and was exposed in 2005 and 2006.

Autumn and winter holidays, by date.Halloween: Grew from the ancient Celtic festival Samhain. Its name is short for All Hallows' Eve, the night before All Saints' Day.
Autumn and winter holidays, by date.All Saints' Day: Honors all saints, known and unknown. In Mexico it opens the Day of the Dead celebrations, which run into the next day.
Autumn and winter holidays, by date.All Souls' Day: Prayers for the dead. In medieval England the poor went 'souling' for soul cakes, an early ancestor of trick-or-treating.
Autumn and winter holidays, by date.Guy Fawkes Night: Marks the failed Gunpowder Plot of 1605 to blow up Parliament. Britons light bonfires and burn effigies of the plotter.
Autumn and winter holidays, by date.Armistice Day: Marks the 1918 ceasefire that ended fighting in World War I at the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month.
Autumn and winter holidays, by date.US Thanksgiving: Its date drifts between the 22nd and 28th of November. Abraham Lincoln proclaimed it a national holiday in 1863.
Autumn and winter holidays, by date.St Andrew's Day: Patron saint of Scotland, whose X-shaped cross gives the Scottish flag its saltire design. Romania also claims him.
Autumn and winter holidays, by date.St Nicholas Day: The real 4th-century bishop of Myra behind Santa Claus. Dutch and German children leave out shoes to be filled with treats.
Autumn and winter holidays, by date.Christmas Eve: In Germany and Scandinavia the main gift-opening happens this evening rather than on the 25th.
Autumn and winter holidays, by date.Boxing Day: In Britain it may take its name from servants' Christmas boxes. It is now famous for sales and football fixtures.

Digital size: from one letter to a libra.One text character: A single byte holds one basic letter and can take 256 different values, making it the building block of nearly every file you open.
Digital size: from one letter to a libra.A max-length tweet (text): Twitter originally capped posts at 140 characters, a nod to SMS limits, and doubled the cap to 280 in 2017.
Digital size: from one letter to a libra.Tetris on the Game Boy: Game Boy Tetris squeezed into a 32 KB cartridge, tiny by today's standards, yet it sold around 35 million copies.
Digital size: from one letter to a libra.Commodore 64 memory: Released in 1982, it became the best-selling single computer model of all time, by most counts well over ten million units.
Digital size: from one letter to a libra.3.5-inch floppy disk: Despite the name, the 3.5-inch disk had a rigid plastic shell, and its 1.44 MB was enough for a short novel.
Digital size: from one letter to a libra.Shakespeare's works (text): Shakespeare's complete works come to only about 5 MB of plain text, less than one percent of what a single CD holds.
Digital size: from one letter to a libra.Audio CD: A CD holds about 80 minutes of music, and legend says its size was chosen so Beethoven's Ninth would fit on one disc.
Digital size: from one letter to a libra.DVD (single layer): A single-layer DVD holds a full movie, and dual-layer versions double the capacity to about 8.5 GB.
Digital size: from one letter to a libra.Blu-ray (single layer): A Blu-ray disc holds about 25 GB per layer, and the format won a format war against HD DVD that ended in 2008.
Digital size: from one letter to a libra.Library of Congress books: Even the Library of Congress's books, as plain text, would fit on a few shelves of hard drives, though estimates of this are rough.

Count the sides (or faces).Möbius strip: It has just one side and one edge, and cutting it down the middle yields one long loop, not two.
Count the sides (or faces).Yield sign: The inverted triangle is used for yield signs in many countries and stands out as unique among road signs.
Count the sides (or faces).The Pentagon: The US defense headquarters took its shape from an original site bounded by five roads, and the shape stuck.
Count the sides (or faces).Honeycomb cell: Bees build hexagons because they tile without gaps and use the least wax.
Count the sides (or faces).UK 50p coin: Introduced in 1969, it was the first seven-sided coin, easy to tell apart by touch.
Count the sides (or faces).Stop sign: Drivers can recognize it from behind, and some countries write STOP in local language.
Count the sides (or faces).Canadian loonie: Introduced in 1987, it got its name from the loon on its back.
Count the sides (or faces).Old British threepenny bit: The brass coin was introduced in 1937 and ended when Britain decimalised in 1971.
Count the sides (or faces).Icosahedron die (D&D): Dungeons & Dragons players roll it to decide whether attacks hit.
Count the sides (or faces).Classic soccer ball: The 12 pentagons and 20 hexagons are a pattern chemists found in the carbon molecule buckyball.

Extinct beasts by weight.Dodo: This flightless pigeon relative lived only on Mauritius and vanished within about a century of sailors' arrival, along with introduced pigs and rats.
Extinct beasts by weight.Thylacine: The last captive animal died in Hobart Zoo in 1936, and this striped marsupial hunter is often called the Tasmanian tiger.
Extinct beasts by weight.Dire wolf: DNA studies show this Ice Age predator was a separate lineage from gray wolves, despite the look of a stocky wolf.
Extinct beasts by weight.Smilodon: Often called the sabre-toothed tiger, it was not a tiger at all, and thousands of its bones were pulled from the La Brea Tar Pits.
Extinct beasts by weight.Short-faced bear: Long-legged and huge, this Ice Age North American bear stood taller than any modern bear when upright, and probably ran fast.
Extinct beasts by weight.Woolly rhino: Ice Age artists painted this horned giant on cave walls in Europe, and frozen carcasses show its thick fur.
Extinct beasts by weight.Megatherium (ground sloth): This ground sloth was the size of an elephant, and it could rear up on its hind legs and tail to reach tree leaves.
Extinct beasts by weight.Woolly mammoth: A small population survived on Wrangel Island until about 4,000 years ago, long after the Egyptian pyramids were built.
Extinct beasts by weight.Columbian mammoth: Larger than its woolly cousin, it lived in the warmer south of North America, and sported huge, curved tusks.
Extinct beasts by weight.Paraceratherium: A hornless rhino relative that lived in Asia about 30 million years ago, it stood about 5 m at the shoulder and is possibly the largest land mammal ever.

When these sitcoms first aired.I Love Lucy: It pioneered filming with several cameras in front of a live audience, so reruns looked sharp and still run decades later.
When these sitcoms first aired.The Brady Bunch: It was never a ratings hit in its original run, but reruns turned the blended family into a cultural fixture.
When these sitcoms first aired.Happy Days: Henry Winkler's Fonzie began as a minor character but became so popular that the show spawned Mork & Mindy and Laverne & Shirley.
When these sitcoms first aired.Cheers: The Boston bar of the show was inspired by the Bull & Finch pub, and the series spawned Frasier.
When these sitcoms first aired.The Golden Girls: It won the Emmy for best comedy series in its first two seasons, with four women sharing a Miami house.
When these sitcoms first aired.Seinfeld: It was famously 'a show about nothing', created by Larry David and Jerry Seinfeld, and its finale came in 1998.
When these sitcoms first aired.Friends: The finale in 2004 drew about 52 million American viewers, one of the biggest television audiences ever.
When these sitcoms first aired.The Office (US): It adapted the British series by Ricky Gervais and Stephen Merchant, but outlasted it by many seasons.
When these sitcoms first aired.The Big Bang Theory: It ran 12 seasons and 279 episodes, and its lead character Sheldon later got a prequel, Young Sheldon.
When these sitcoms first aired.Modern Family: This mockumentary-style sitcom won five Emmys in a row for outstanding comedy series, from 2011 to 2015.

Famous chess games and matches.The Immortal Game: Adolf Anderssen sacrificed both rooks, a bishop and his queen before mating with his remaining pieces.
Famous chess games and matches.The Opera Game: Paul Morphy beat two amateur allies in 17 moves in a box at the Paris Opera while Norma played.
Famous chess games and matches.Fischer's Game of the Century: Thirteen-year-old Bobby Fischer sacrificed his queen to beat Donald Byrne in a game still studied today.
Famous chess games and matches.Fischer vs Spassky: The match in Reykjavik ended Soviet dominance of the title, a hold that had lasted since 1948.
Famous chess games and matches.Karpov-Kasparov endless match: The match was halted after five months and 48 games with no winner, and the controversy brought a restart.
Famous chess games and matches.Deep Blue beats Kasparov: IBM's machine beat the reigning world champion in a match for the first time under standard conditions, 3.5 to 2.5.
Famous chess games and matches.Kasparov's Immortal: Kasparov sacrificed a rook to Veselin Topalov at Wijk aan Zee and launched an attack that is still celebrated.
Famous chess games and matches.Judit Polgar beats Kasparov: Polgar, widely seen as the strongest woman player ever, beat the former world champion in a Moscow rapid game.
Famous chess games and matches.Carlsen's first world title: Magnus Carlsen beat Viswanathan Anand in Chennai at 22 and held the title until 2023, when he chose not to defend.
Famous chess games and matches.AlphaZero crushes Stockfish: DeepMind's AI taught itself chess from the rules in hours and beat Stockfish in a 100-game match with no losses.

Eponyms: when the namesake person was bo.Nicotine (Jean Nicot): Jean Nicot, French ambassador in Lisbon, sent tobacco to the French court in the 1560s as a medicine.
Eponyms: when the namesake person was bo.Silhouette (Étienne de S.): The French finance minister's austerity made cheap shadow portraits, which carried his name as a joke.
Eponyms: when the namesake person was bo.Sandwich (the Earl): Legend says the 4th Earl asked for meat between bread so he could keep gambling, and Hawaii was once named the Sandwich Islands for him.
Eponyms: when the namesake person was bo.Mesmerize (Franz Mesmer): A royal commission including Benjamin Franklin tested his 'animal magnetism' and found nothing to it.
Eponyms: when the namesake person was bo.Guillotine (Dr Guillotin): Dr Joseph-Ignace Guillotin only proposed a humane way to execute, and he disliked having his name attached to it.
Eponyms: when the namesake person was bo.Shrapnel (Henry Shrapnel): Henry Shrapnel, a British officer, designed an artillery shell packed with balls in the 1780s.
Eponyms: when the namesake person was bo.Braille (Louis Braille): He was blinded as a child and devised his system at 15, inspired by a military code for reading at night.
Eponyms: when the namesake person was bo.Saxophone (Adolphe Sax): The Belgian instrument maker patented his instrument in 1846 and also invented the saxhorn.
Eponyms: when the namesake person was bo.Boycott (Charles Boycott): Captain Charles Boycott, a land agent in County Mayo, was shunned by his tenants in 1880 over rents.
Eponyms: when the namesake person was bo.Diesel (Rudolf Diesel): The inventor vanished from a steamer crossing the Channel in 1913 and was never found.

How salty is the water?.Don Juan Pond, Antarctica: Its calcium chloride brine stays liquid even at around minus 50 degrees Celsius.
How salty is the water?.Dead Sea: It is about nine times saltier than the sea, so swimmers float, and its shore is the lowest land on Earth.
How salty is the water?.Great Salt Lake: Its saltiness changes with the water level, and only brine shrimp and flies thrive in it.
How salty is the water?.Red Sea: With heat, high evaporation and almost no river inflow, it is saltier than the average ocean.
How salty is the water?.Average ocean: Most of the sea's salt came from rocks on land, carried to it by rivers over millions of years.
How salty is the water?.Black Sea: Below about 150 metres it holds almost no oxygen, because it mixes poorly with the water above.
How salty is the water?.Caspian Sea: It is the world's largest inland body of water, and is salty but far less so than the oceans.
How salty is the water?.Baltic Sea: A mix of fresh river water and salt water from the North Sea makes this brackish, a home to both marine and freshwater species.
How salty is the water?.Lake Baikal: The deepest lake on Earth, over 1,600 metres, holds about a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water.
How salty is the water?.Rainwater: It is close to pure, yet slightly acidic, because carbon dioxide dissolves in it.

How long these famous captivities lasted.Trapped Chilean miners: Thirty-three miners were trapped 700 m underground in Chile, and all were rescued one by one in 2010.
How long these famous captivities lasted.Iran hostage crisis: Fifty-two Americans were held in Tehran until minutes after Ronald Reagan took office in January 1981.
How long these famous captivities lasted.Anne Frank in hiding: Anne Frank spent two years in the Secret Annex above an Amsterdam warehouse; her father later published her diary.
How long these famous captivities lasted.Dreyfus on Devil's Island: The French army officer was wrongly convicted of treason, and Émile Zola's 'J'accuse' helped lead to his exoneration.
How long these famous captivities lasted.Napoleon on St. Helena: After Waterloo, he was sent to a remote South Atlantic island, where he stayed until his death in 1821.
How long these famous captivities lasted.Galileo's house arrest: The astronomer was kept under house arrest after the Inquisition tried him for supporting a Sun-centred universe.
How long these famous captivities lasted.Mary, Queen of Scots: She was held by her cousin Elizabeth I for years, until a plot linked her to a plan to take the throne.
How long these famous captivities lasted.Nelson Mandela: He spent 18 of those years on Robben Island, and later became South Africa's first democratically elected president.
How long these famous captivities lasted.Man in the Iron Mask: He was a prisoner of Louis XIV, and the mask was reportedly black velvet, not the iron of legend.
How long these famous captivities lasted.Rudolf Hess: Hitler's deputy flew to Scotland in 1941 and was jailed for life; later he was Spandau Prison's only inmate.

How loud is it?.Breathing: At the edge of silence, breathing is barely audible. The scale is logarithmic, so every 10 dB is ten times the sound power.
How loud is it?.Rustling leaves: A quiet forest has about this much noise, and it is one of the quietest everyday sounds.
How loud is it?.Whisper: Hearing a whisper at arm's length is near this level, and a library is not much louder.
How loud is it?.Quiet fridge hum: Fridges hum at roughly this level, which is why you notice it when the room goes quiet.
How loud is it?.Normal conversation: Normal speech at about a metre is about 60 dB, comfortable for hours.
How loud is it?.Vacuum cleaner: Daily exposure to this sort of noise over years can start to harm hearing.
How loud is it?.Lawn mower: Hearing damage can begin after a couple of hours at this level, so ear protection is advised.
How loud is it?.Rock concert: Without ear protection, listening for just a few minutes can begin to damage hearing.
How loud is it?.Jet engine, up close: Pain starts around 120 dB, so this is far beyond it, and ear protection is vital.
How loud is it?.Krakatoa, 160 km away: The 1883 eruption was heard thousands of kilometres away, and is often called the loudest sound in recorded history.

Big ideas and discoveries in astronomy.Copernicus: Sun-centered: He reportedly saw the first printed copy of 'De revolutionibus' on his deathbed, the year it was published.
Big ideas and discoveries in astronomy.Kepler's first laws: Using Tycho Brahe's Mars data, he showed planets travel in ellipses, not circles, which broke with 2,000 years of tradition.
Big ideas and discoveries in astronomy.Newton's Principia: Isaac Newton's work laid out the laws of motion and gravitation, and Edmond Halley paid for its printing.
Big ideas and discoveries in astronomy.Halley predicts his comet: He noticed comets in 1531, 1607 and 1682 were likely one object and predicted its 1758 return, years after his death.
Big ideas and discoveries in astronomy.Hubble: universe expanding: Edwin Hubble used pulsating Cepheid stars to show galaxies recede, with more distant ones moving faster.
Big ideas and discoveries in astronomy.Quasars identified: Maarten Schmidt realised the faint point 3C 273 was extremely distant, so it must outshine whole galaxies; black holes power such quasars.
Big ideas and discoveries in astronomy.Cosmic microwave background: Two Bell Labs engineers chasing a stubborn hiss in a horn antenna found the Big Bang's afterglow, winning a Nobel in 1978.
Big ideas and discoveries in astronomy.Pulsars discovered: Jocelyn Bell Burnell spotted regular radio pulses so precise that they were jokingly labelled LGM-1 for 'little green men'.
Big ideas and discoveries in astronomy.Expansion is accelerating: Distant exploding stars looked dimmer than expected, hinting at dark energy; the finding won a Nobel Prize in 2011.
Big ideas and discoveries in astronomy.Gravitational waves detected: LIGO caught ripples from two black holes merging over a billion light-years away, a century after Einstein predicted them.

Holiday foods through the calendar year.Galette des rois (Epiphany): A cake with a hidden bean or figurine, the fève. Whoever finds it becomes king or queen for the day.
Holiday foods through the calendar year.Valentine's chocolates: Richard Cadbury sold the first heart-shaped chocolate box in the 1860s, linking sweets with Valentine's Day.
Holiday foods through the calendar year.St. Patrick's corned beef: In Ireland the traditional dish was bacon. Irish immigrants in the US swapped it for cheaper corned beef.
Holiday foods through the calendar year.Swedish Midsummer strawberries: The Swedes eat strawberries and cream with the first new potatoes and herring at midsummer.
Holiday foods through the calendar year.US Independence Day hot dogs: Americans eat around 150 million hot dogs on the Fourth of July, according to the industry's trade group.
Holiday foods through the calendar year.Oktoberfest beer (opening): Despite the name, Oktoberfest begins in September, when the Munich mayor taps the first keg with 'O'zapft is!'.
Holiday foods through the calendar year.Halloween candy: The custom of trick-or-treating has roots in medieval 'souling' and Scottish 'guising', where people went door to door.
Holiday foods through the calendar year.US Thanksgiving turkey: Tens of millions of turkeys are eaten at US Thanksgiving, a tradition tied to 19th-century proclamations.
Holiday foods through the calendar year.Christmas pudding: Traditionally made weeks earlier on 'Stir-up Sunday', often with a silver coin hidden for luck.
Holiday foods through the calendar year.New Year's Eve Champagne: A popped cork can leave the bottle at around 50 km/h, which is why you should point it away.

Drink sizes.Shot of espresso: A single shot is only about 30 ml; 'espresso' means 'pressed out' in Italian, for how hot water is forced through the coffee.
Drink sizes.Starbucks Demi: Demitasse is French for 'half cup', and this tiny size is meant for a concentrated sip rather than a long drink.
Drink sizes.Starbucks Short: This was Starbucks' original small size, and it is now tucked off the main menu, available only if you ask.
Drink sizes.Starbucks Tall: Despite the name, 'tall' is the small on the menu, which is why the Italian-style size names confuse newcomers.
Drink sizes.Starbucks Grande: Grande is Italian for 'large', yet at 16 ounces it is the middle size, a quirk of Starbucks' naming.
Drink sizes.Starbucks Venti (hot): Venti means 'twenty' in Italian, matching the 20 ounces of a hot cup, a size added after Grande to cater for big drinkers.
Drink sizes.Starbucks Venti (iced): The iced venti is bigger than the hot one, 24 ounces instead of 20, because it must leave room for ice.
Drink sizes.Standard wine bottle: A standard bottle is 750 ml, which pours about five glasses of wine, and which became standard in Europe in the 20th century.
Drink sizes.Starbucks Trenta: Trenta is Italian for 'thirty', and the size is offered only for certain cold drinks, since a hot one would be too big to sip.
Drink sizes.Magnum wine bottle: A magnum holds two standard bottles, 1.5 liters, and bigger bottles carry biblical names such as Jeroboam and Methuselah.

When these eponymous conditions were fir.Parkinson's disease: James Parkinson described the 'shaking palsy' in an 1817 essay; Jean-Martin Charcot later gave the disease his name.
When these eponymous conditions were fir.Hodgkin's lymphoma: Thomas Hodgkin noticed the pattern in 1832 at Guy's Hospital in London; his name was attached only decades later by others.
When these eponymous conditions were fir.Graves' disease: Irish physician Robert Graves described this overactive-thyroid disease; in Germany it is called Basedow's disease instead.
When these eponymous conditions were fir.Down syndrome: John Langdon Down described it in 1866, but the extra copy of chromosome 21 behind it was only identified in 1959.
When these eponymous conditions were fir.Huntington's disease: George Huntington was only 22 when he described this inherited disorder in 1872, drawing on patients his father and grandfather had treated.
When these eponymous conditions were fir.Tourette syndrome: Georges Gilles de la Tourette, a student of Charcot, described the tics and vocal outbursts in French patients in 1885.
When these eponymous conditions were fir.Alzheimer's disease: Alois Alzheimer presented the case of Auguste Deter in 1906; her brain showed the plaques and tangles still used to define the disease.
When these eponymous conditions were fir.Cushing's disease: Harvey Cushing, a pioneering American neurosurgeon, described this condition of excess cortisol in 1912; he also brought blood-pressure monitoring to US surgery.
When these eponymous conditions were fir.Crohn's disease: Burrill Crohn and two Mount Sinai colleagues described it in 1932; his name led the paper's author list, so it stuck.
When these eponymous conditions were fir.Asperger syndrome: Hans Asperger described socially awkward but gifted children in 1944; his work stayed little known in English until Lorna Wing popularized it in 1981.

In one year: how many of each?.Solstices: The summer and winter solstices mark the longest and shortest days. At Stonehenge, crowds still gather to watch the sun rise on the midsummer one.
In one year: how many of each?.Seasons: Seasons come from Earth's tilt, not its distance from the Sun. Earth is actually closest to the Sun in early January, during the northern winter.
In one year: how many of each?.Months: The English names for July and August honour Julius Caesar and Augustus. September to December once meant the seventh to tenth months, hence their Latin roots.
In one year: how many of each?.Fortnights: The word comes from the old English for fourteen nights. It is common in British English, though many Americans do not use it.
In one year: how many of each?.Weeks: The seven-day week has ancient Babylonian and Jewish roots and is not tied to any astronomical cycle. France briefly tried a ten-day week after its revolution.
In one year: how many of each?.Days: A year is really about 365.24 days, which is why we add a leap day every four years. Without it, the calendar would drift away from the seasons.
In one year: how many of each?.Hours: Dividing the day into 24 hours goes back to ancient Egyptians, who split daytime and night-time into twelve parts each.
In one year: how many of each?.Minutes: The song Seasons of Love in the musical Rent opens by counting 525,600 minutes in a year. The word minute comes from the Latin for a tiny part.
In one year: how many of each?.Seconds: The second was once defined as a fraction of a day, but since 1967 it has been defined by the vibrations of a caesium atom.
In one year: how many of each?.Resting heartbeats: A resting adult heart beats around 70 times a minute, which adds up to tens of millions of beats a year. Over a lifetime, it's about 2.5 billion.

Jack and the Beanstalk, in story order.Jack sets off to sell the cow: Joseph Jacobs's 1890 retelling made Jack and the Beanstalk famous in English, though the tale was already in print earlier in the 1800s.
Jack and the Beanstalk, in story order.Swaps the cow for magic beans: The trade looks foolish, which is the point: fairy tales love rewarding the underestimated, poor or youngest hero.
Jack and the Beanstalk, in story order.Mother throws the beans away: Her anger sets up the payoff, a classic fairy-tale reversal in which the thing thrown away turns out to be the treasure.
Jack and the Beanstalk, in story order.A giant beanstalk grows: Real climbing beans can grow several metres in a season, so a stalk that reaches the clouds only exaggerates what the plant already does.
Jack and the Beanstalk, in story order.Jack climbs into the clouds: Sky-realms of giants echo old myths, from Norse Jotunheim to Greek Olympus.
Jack and the Beanstalk, in story order.\"Fee-fi-fo-fum!\": Shakespeare quotes the chant in King Lear: Fie, foh, and fum, I smell the blood of a British man.
Jack and the Beanstalk, in story order.Jack grabs a bag of gold: Some tellers make the giant the real thief, saying he stole Jack's father's riches, which gives Jack moral cover for the theft.
Jack and the Beanstalk, in story order.Jack takes the golden hen: A hen laying golden eggs echoes Aesop's fable of the goose that laid golden eggs, a warning about greed.
Jack and the Beanstalk, in story order.Jack takes the singing harp: In Jacobs's telling the harp calls out Master! Master! as Jack escapes, giving the giant a clue.
Jack and the Beanstalk, in story order.Jack chops down the beanstalk: Chopping the stalk ends the giant's pursuit, and in most versions he crashes to the ground and Jack's family is safe and rich.

Disney's Pinocchio, in story order.Geppetto wishes on a star: When You Wish Upon a Star won an Oscar and became Disney's signature tune.
Disney's Pinocchio, in story order.Blue Fairy brings him to life: Carlo Collodi wrote Pinocchio in 1881 to 1883 as a serial in an Italian children's newspaper.
Disney's Pinocchio, in story order.Jiminy becomes his conscience: Jiminy Cricket is Disney's creation; Collodi's talking cricket is squashed by Pinocchio early on.
Disney's Pinocchio, in story order.Honest John lures him away: Honest John is a sly fox who lures Pinocchio to Stromboli with the song Hi-Diddle-Dee-Dee.
Disney's Pinocchio, in story order.Stromboli locks him in a cage: Stromboli is also the name of an Italian volcanic island; Collodi's puppeteer is Mangiafuoco, meaning fire-eater.
Disney's Pinocchio, in story order.His nose grows as he lies: The growing nose is Collodi's idea, and in the book it first happens when he lies to the Blue Fairy.
Disney's Pinocchio, in story order.Off to Pleasure Island: Pleasure Island's boys smoke and play pool in a darker part of Disney's 1940 film.
Disney's Pinocchio, in story order.Boys turn into donkeys: In Collodi's book the boys turn into donkeys after months of fun in Toyland, and Pinocchio is sold as a working donkey.
Disney's Pinocchio, in story order.Swallowed by Monstro: Monstro is a whale, but in Collodi's book he is a giant shark known as the Terrible Dogfish.
Disney's Pinocchio, in story order.He becomes a real boy: In Collodi's 1883 book he becomes a real boy by caring for his father, a more moral ending than Disney's.

When these pizza chains began.Pizzeria Uno: Chicago's famous deep-dish pizza was born at this restaurant, founded by Ike Sewell and Ric Riccardo.
When these pizza chains began.Shakey's Pizza: Often credited as the first pizza franchise, it combined pizza with beer halls and banjo music.
When these pizza chains began.Sbarro: It started as an Italian grocery in Brooklyn and is most famous for mall food courts.
When these pizza chains began.Pizza Hut: Two Wichita brothers, Dan and Frank Carney, opened it with a loan from their mother, and the name fit the small sign.
When these pizza chains began.Little Caesars: Founded in Michigan by Mike and Marian Ilitch; Mike later also owned the Detroit Tigers and Red Wings.
When these pizza chains began.Domino's: Tom Monaghan bought a small Michigan pizzeria with his brother, and the chain became known for guaranteed delivery times.
When these pizza chains began.Chuck E. Cheese's: Founded by Atari's Nolan Bushnell, the first one opened in San Jose as Pizza Time Theatre.
When these pizza chains began.Papa Murphy's: It pioneered take-and-bake pizza, which you finish cooking at home.
When these pizza chains began.Papa John's: John Schnatter started by selling pizza from a closet in his father's tavern after selling his car.
When these pizza chains began.MOD Pizza: Founded in Seattle by Scott and Ally Svenson, with a build-your-own concept; MOD stands for Made On Demand.
